title: Create a Repository Git Tree
knowledge:
# Create a Repository Git Tree

## Prerequisites

- You must have access to the target repository (sufficient permissions to create Git objects in the repo).

## Method

`POST`

## URL

`https://api.github.com/repos/{{owner}}/{{repo}}/git/trees`

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
```

## Description

Creates a new Git tree object in a repository. The tree creation API accepts nested entries. If you specify both a tree and a nested path modifying that tree, this endpoint overwrites the contents of the tree with the new path contents and creates a new tree structure.

If you use this endpoint to add, delete, or modify file contents in a tree, you must create a commit from the tree and then update a branch reference to point to the new commit. Returns an error if you try to delete a file that does not exist.

## Enforcement Rules

- The `owner` path parameter **must always be present**.
- The `repo` path parameter **must always be present**.
- Always construct the path as `/repos/{{owner}}/{{repo}}/git/trees`, where `{{owner}}` and `{{repo}}` are **non-empty strings**.
- Do **not** call the API with missing or empty path parameters (e.g., avoid `/repos//my-repo/git/trees`, `/repos/octo-org//git/trees`, or `/repos/octo-org/my-repo/git/trees` missing segments).
- Do **not** infer or guess `owner` or `repo` beyond what the user provides.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Path Parameters** in the URL and **not in the body**.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Query Parameters** in the URL as query parameters and **not in the body** (this endpoint has no documented query parameters).

### Valid Examples

```http
/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees
/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/trees
```

### Invalid Examples

```http
/repos//hello-world/git/trees
/repos/octo-org//git/trees
/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees/
```

## Required Path Parameters

| Parameter | Type   | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `owner`  | string | The account owner of the repository. Not case sensitive. |
| `repo`   | string | The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. Not case sensitive. |

## Required Request Body Fields

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `tree`   | array | Objects specifying a tree structure. Each entry may include `path`, `mode`, `type`, `sha`, `content`. |

## Optional Request Body Fields

| Parameter   | Type   | Description |
|------------|--------|-------------|
| `base_tree` | string | SHA1 of an existing Git tree object used as the base for the new tree. Entries in `tree` overwrite items from `base_tree` with the same `path`. If omitted, GitHub creates a new tree only from `tree`. If you later commit this tree, files from the parent commit’s tree that are not included in `tree` will be listed as deleted by the new commit. |

## `tree[]` Entry Fields

| Parameter | Type   | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `path`   | string | The file referenced in the tree. |
| `mode`   | string | File mode. One of: `100644` (file/blob), `100755` (executable/blob), `040000` (subdirectory/tree), `160000` (submodule/commit), `120000` (symlink/blob). |
| `type`   | string | One of: `blob`, `tree`, `commit`. |
| `sha`    | string | SHA1 of the object in the tree (also called `tree.sha`). If `null`, the file will be deleted. **Note:** Use either `sha` or `content` to specify contents. Using both returns an error. |
| `content`| string | Content to write for this file; GitHub writes a blob and uses its SHA for this entry. **Note:** Use either `content` or `sha`. Using both returns an error. |

## Response

### Success Response (201 Created)

Headers may include:

- `Location`: string

```json
{
  "sha": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees/9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
  "truncated": false,
  "tree": [
    {
      "path": "file.rb",
      "mode": "100644",
      "type": "blob",
      "sha": "44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132",
      "size": 132,
      "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/blobs/44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Error Response (403 Forbidden)

```json
{
  "message": "Forbidden",
  "documentation_url": "https://docs.github.com/rest",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees",
  "status": "403"
}
```

### Error Response (404 Resource not found)

```json
{
  "message": "Not Found",
  "documentation_url": "https://docs.github.com/rest",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees",
  "status": "404"
}
```

### Error Response (409 Conflict)

```json
{
  "message": "Conflict",
  "documentation_url": "https://docs.github.com/rest",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees",
  "status": "409"
}
```

### Error Response (422 Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.)

```json
{
  "message": "Validation Failed",
  "documentation_url": "https://docs.github.com/rest",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "Tree",
      "field": "tree",
      "message": "Invalid tree entry",
      "code": "invalid",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "file.rb"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `sha` | string | SHA1 of the created tree. |
| `url` | string | API URL for the created tree. |
| `truncated` | boolean | Indicates whether the returned tree was truncated. |
| `tree` | array | Objects specifying the created tree structure. |
| `tree[].path` | string | Path for the entry. |
| `tree[].mode` | string | Mode for the entry. |
| `tree[].type` | string | Type for the entry (`blob`, `tree`, `commit`). |
| `tree[].sha` | string | SHA1 for the entry. |
| `tree[].size` | integer | Size of the entry (when provided). |
| `tree[].url` | string | API URL for the entry (when provided). |

## Sample Request

```bash
curl -i --request POST \
  'https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "base_tree": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
    "tree": [
      {
        "path": "file.rb",
        "mode": "100644",
        "type": "blob",
        "sha": "44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## Example Usage

### Example 1: Create a tree based on an existing tree SHA

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "base_tree": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
    "tree": [
      { "path": "file.rb", "mode": "100644", "type": "blob", "sha": "44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132" }
    ]
  }'
```

### Example 2: Create/update a file by providing `content` (instead of `sha`)

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "base_tree": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
    "tree": [
      { "path": "README.md", "mode": "100644", "type": "blob", "content": "# Hello World\n" }
    ]
  }'
```

### Example 3: Delete a file by setting `sha` to `null`

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/hello-world/git/trees' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "base_tree": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
    "tree": [
      { "path": "old.txt", "mode": "100644", "type": "blob", "sha": null }
    ]
  }'
```

## Behavior

1. Validates `owner`/`repo` and the request body structure.
2. If `base_tree` is provided, starts from that tree; otherwise starts from only the provided `tree` entries.
3. Applies entries in `tree`; entries with the same `path` overwrite existing ones from `base_tree`.
4. If `sha` is `null`, attempts to delete the file (errors if the file does not exist).
5. Returns the created tree SHA and the resulting tree listing (may be truncated).

## Notes

- The endpoint accepts nested entries; overlapping nested paths can overwrite prior contents.
- To apply the tree to a branch, you must:
  1) create a commit using the new tree, then  
  2) update a reference to point to that commit.
- For `tree[]` entries, use **either** `sha` **or** `content` to set contents; providing both returns an error.

## Gotchas

- If you omit `base_tree` and later commit the resulting tree, files from the parent commit’s tree that are not included in `tree` will appear as deleted in the new commit.
- Deleting a non-existent file (using `sha: null`) returns an error.
- Providing both `sha` and `content` for the same `tree[]` entry returns an error.

## Error Handling

- **403 Forbidden**: Not allowed to access or modify the repository.
- **404 Not Found**: Repository (or resource) not found.
- **409 Conflict**: Conflict creating the tree (as returned by the API).
- **422 Unprocessable Entity**: Validation failed or the endpoint has been spammed; includes an `errors[]` array with details.
